title: -ing and -ed clauses (the woman talking to Tom, the boy injured in the accident)
subtitle: the woman talking to Tom
summary: Use an -ing clause to say what somebody or something is doing, and an -ed clause with a passive meaning, to add information after a noun.

lesson.heading: -ing clauses
lesson.text: A clause is a part of a sentence. Some clauses begin with **-ing**: *Who is the woman **talking to Tom**?* We use an -ing clause to say what somebody or something **is** (or **was**) doing at a particular time.

examples.text: Who is the woman **talking to Tom**?
examples.note: the woman is talking to Tom

examples.text: Police **investigating the crime** are looking for three men.
I was woken up by a bell **ringing**.

lesson.heading: -ing clauses for things that are always true
lesson.text: You can also use an **-ing** clause to say what happens all the time, not just at one particular moment.

examples.text: The road **connecting the two villages** is very narrow.
examples.note: the road connects the two villages

examples.text: I have a large room **overlooking the garden**.
Can you think of the name of a flower **beginning with T**?

lesson.heading: -ed clauses
lesson.text: Some clauses begin with a past participle: *The boy **injured in the accident** was taken to hospital.* These **-ed** clauses have a **passive** meaning.

examples.text: The boy **injured in the accident** was taken to hospital.
examples.note: he was injured in the accident

examples.text: George showed me some pictures **painted by his father**.
examples.note: they were painted by his father

examples.text: The gun **used in the robbery** has been found.
examples.note: the gun was used in the robbery

lesson.heading: -ing or -ed?

left.label: -ing (active)
left.text: The person or thing does the action.
examples: The taxi **taking us to the airport** broke down.
Life is unpleasant for people **living near busy airports**.
I received an email **offering me the job**.

right.label: -ed (passive)
right.text: The action is done to the person or thing.
examples: The paintings **stolen from the museum** haven't been found.
We've repaired the gate **damaged in the storm**.
Most of the suggestions **made at the meeting** were not practical.

lesson.note: Most past participles end in -ed, but many are irregular: **stolen, made, built, blown, written**.

lesson.heading: there is / there was + -ing or -ed
lesson.text: You can use **there is / there was** etc. with -ing and -ed clauses. We also use **left** in this way, meaning *not used, still there*.

examples.text: There were some children **swimming** in the river.
There was a big red car **parked** outside the house.
We've eaten nearly all the chocolates. There are only a few **left**.

lesson.text: Ask yourself: is the noun doing the action or receiving it? Doing it takes -ing, receiving it takes the past participle.

exercises.prompt: A bell was ringing and it woke me up. I was woken up by a bell ___.
exercises.explanation: The bell was doing the action, so we use the -ing form.

exercises.prompt: George showed me some pictures ___ by his father.
exercises.explanation: The pictures were painted by his father - a passive meaning, so we use the past participle.

exercises.statement: Most of the goods made in this factory are exported.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The goods are made in the factory, so the -ed clause with a passive meaning is right.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence beginning with the -ed clause that completes it.

pairs.left: The paintings ... haven't been found yet.
Most of the suggestions ... were not practical.
Our friends live in a beautiful house ... .

exercises.prompt: Life must be very unpleasant for people ___ near busy airports.
exercises.explanation: The people live near the airports, so the clause is active: -ing.

exercises.prompt: A taxi was taking us to the airport and it broke down. The taxi ___ us to the airport broke down.
exercises.explanation: The taxi was taking us, so the -ing clause is right.

exercises.prompt: A few days after the interview, I received an email ___ me the job.
exercises.explanation: The email offered me the job, so the clause is active: offering.

exercises.prompt: The building was badly damaged in a fire ___ by an electrical fault.
exercises.explanation: The fire was caused by a fault - a passive meaning, so we use caused.

exercises.prompt: Did you see the picture of the trees ___ down in the storm?
exercises.explanation: The trees were blown down. Blow is irregular: the past participle is blown.

exercises.prompt: The college offers English courses in the evening and a course begins next Monday. Say this with There.
exercises.answer: There's a course beginning next Monday
exercises.explanation: There is / there was can be followed by a noun + an -ing clause.

exercises.prompt: I've spent all the money I had. There's ___.
exercises.explanation: Left here means not used, still there - and here there is none.

exercises.statement: The piece of paper was blank. There was nothing wrote on it.
exercises.explanation: There was nothing written on it. We need the past participle written, not the past simple wrote.
